messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Flat and unrealistic predict output from LGCP inlabru model
parts:
Based on the plot, it's not actually flat at all, but rather has a
huge spike at a boundary location.
Check to make sure that there are no observed points outside the
specified samplers region.
Finn

On Wed, 29 Jun 2022 at 15:03, Tom Pienkowski
<pienkows...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hello all,
>
> My issue looks similar to that discussed in the 2018 thread (here), but I've been unable to resolve the below problem despite following its advice.
>
> I am using inlabru to run an LGCP on hunting trap locations with an SPDE. The predicted intensity is very high and flat as can be seen in the attached.
>
> Based on the previous thread, I'd:
>
> Created the "samplers" domain from the mesh itself, so there was no mismatch between them.
> In doing so, I had to simplify the input boundary in an attempt to remove apparent self intersection (but it persists). This included using gSimplify and gBuffer prior to creating the mesh.
> Removed the CRS.
>
> The previous thread related to a barrier model, so it appears not all of it applied in my simpler case. But perhaps I've missed something crucial!
>
> The data is sensitive so unfortunately, I can't share it publically but can share it by email if needed. Attached is the code, warnings, and session info.
>
> Any advice would be really appreciated!
>
> Tom
